In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the availability of a system with ‘start up process time’ for a repair facility and imperfect switch is always less than that of a system without these features.
the availability of this system is always less than that of a similar system with perfect switch and the MTSF is always more than that of a perfect switch case.
the ‘start-up process’ has a positive effect on the availability and mean time to failure of the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the system availability is a non-monotonic function of ‘start-up time’ and the system is more reliable when the repair time is small and the start-up time is large and vice versa.
, the availability A ∞ of the two-unit system decreases and the MTSF increases as the ‘start-up time’ of the repair facility and/or the imperfect switch increases.
the availability of the system increases with increase in the repair rate, while it decreases with the increase in the start-up process time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the system is less available when compared with the system with perfect switch.
the availability of a system with imperfect switch can be improved significantly by increasing the repair time of the failed unit.
the system availability is a decreasing function of the repair rate of the repair facility.
